machabu.title: Machabu Byanke & Naamkaran
machabu.text: When a child is born, the household is considered ritually impure (Macha Bu). Between the 4th and 10th day, a purification ceremony called Machabu Byanke is performed by a priest. During this time, the Naamkaran (naming ceremony) is conducted, and the child's birth chart (Jatakam) is prepared by an astrologer.

pasni.title: Macha Janku / Pasni
pasni.text: The infant's first solid food transition. It takes place at 5 or 7 months for girls and 6 or 8 months for boys. The baby is dressed in traditional silk attire, offered rice pudding (Kheer) alongside various traditional dishes, and presented with symbolic items (books, money, soil, jewels) to predict their future inclinations.

childhood.title: Ihi / Kaeta Puja / Bratabandha
childhood.text: Childhood initiation rituals mark a sacred threshold — for girls through Ihi, and for boys through Kaeta Puja and Bratabandha.
childhood.girlsText: Celebrated between ages 5 and 9. The young girl is symbolically married to a Bel fruit (wood apple), representing Lord Suvarna Kumar (a manifestation of Lord Vishnu). Because her first eternal spouse is divine and immortal, a Newar woman is traditionally never considered a widow, even if her human spouse passes away.
childhood.boysTitle: For Boys — Kaeta Puja / Chudakarma / Bare Chuyegu
childhood.boysText: Performed between ages 5 and 13 to mark manhood and clan initiation. A male uncle shaves the boy's head except for a topknot (Tupi). The boy dons yellow mendicant robes, temporarily role-playing as an ascetic monk, before being welcomed back by family to embrace his duties as a householder.

bahra.title: Bahra Chuyegu / Gufa
bahra.text: Before her first menstruation, a girl undergoes 12 days of ritual seclusion in a darkened room, hidden from both sunlight and male family members. Female relatives visit to share wisdom and traditional food. On the 12th day, she is brought out, "married" to the Sun God (Surya), and dressed as a bride to celebrate her transformation into womanhood.

weddings.title: Ihipa / Weddings
weddings.text: Traditional Newar weddings unite two families. A core element is the formal exchange of 10 betel nuts (Lakha) sent from the groom's family to confirm the alliance. The wedding involves elaborate rituals like Honkegu and Chipa Theeke (a ceremony of mutual sharing). Host your reception or marriage banquet in a grand hall built for memorable nights — seating for large guest lists, stage lighting, and dedicated bridal facilities.

janku.title: Janku / Jyah Janko
janku.text: When a Newar individual reaches advanced age, they are elevated to near-divine status through five successive Janku ceremonies. During these events, elders are dressed in royal attire, placed in a wooden chariot (Ratha), and pulled through the town by their children and grandchildren.
stages: Chandraratharohan: 83 years, 4 months, 4 days (Achieves deified status)
